source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: When air or water is heated from below, decide that the heated fluid expands, becomes lighter, rises, and cooler fluid moves down to replace it.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Water at the same warm temperature throughout keeps producing convection currents just because it is warm.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: The lighter heated water sinks, and the heavier cooler water rises to replace it.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: In a solid metal rod heated from below, hot metal particles rise through the rod and cooler ones move down.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Convection begins only when the water boils and bubbles appear.

intelligence.enrichment: In liquids and gases, heat transfer can take place by the actual movement of particles from one place to another; heated fluid expands, becomes lighter, rises, and cooler fluid moves down. Heating a fluid from below makes the lower fluid warmer and lighter, causing upward motion that is replaced by cooler fluid from the sides or above, forming a convection current. The learner correctly applies this rule: In liquids and gases, heat transfer can take place by the actual movement of particles from one place to another; heated fluid expands, becomes lighter, rises, and cooler fluid moves down. Heating water only warms the bottom layer; the rest of the beaker becomes hot without water actually moving.
